correctness.rationale: Starting at (0,1), the two unimodular child maps give the consecutive Stern pair at every index, with leading zeros preserving (0,1). Nonzero pairs modulo seven project to eight states; vanishing numerator means precisely the start state. Constructing the transition matrix M in homogeneous coordinates independently, the (0,0) resolvent coefficient is the corresponding cofactor of I−zM divided by its determinant. Exact cancellation gave the stated rational function, gcd 1 and the partial fractions in RESULT.md lines 74–78. Expanding the denominator reproduces the recurrence; any eventual rational homogeneous recurrence would give a polynomial multiplier making the series polynomial, so must have degree at least six. In the reciprocal quartic, the two real linear coefficients of the displayed quadratics are distinct, have sum 1 and product −4. The sharper bound needed for their discriminants follows from 17<(4√2−1)^2 (equivalently √2<2), not from 17<49 alone as written. Thus all four reciprocal roots are distinct of modulus √2; coprimality leaves nonzero coefficients at each pole. The normalized mean square tends to the nonzero sum of squared coefficients since all cross-ratio geometric means vanish. This proves the limsup, not a pointwise lower bound. Independent replay: `cd /workspace && python checks/independent_replay.py 1` used exact SymPy determinants, rational gcd and partial fractions, and direct Stern counts through r=13 including r=0. The frozen verifier is corroboration; the proof handles every level.
